setupSteps: Pick the version. *Bench-supported (recommended first):* a bench, a firm chair or a sofa seat (it must not slide or tip). Place the left hand and left knee on it (if rowing with the right arm). One source calls this "knee and same-side hand on a flat bench" and notes it helps keep the back flat (snippet). *Staggered-stance, hand on the thigh:* stand with one foot a half-step ahead, rest the free hand on the front thigh just above the knee, and hinge forward. Keep hand contact light so you do not lean on it. One source says the split stance suits people who can hinge with a neutral spine (snippet). *No equipment:* a bottle or rucksack in the working hand, in either stance; or the towel row.
Floor. A non-slip mat on a flat spot; put a folded towel on the floor beside the support to set the weight down on. Put the bench or chair on a rubber mat or against a wall.

Bench version foot and knee placement. The supporting knee sits on the bench directly under the hip; the supporting hand sits flat on the bench under the shoulder, a little ahead of the knee, elbow soft (not locked). The other foot stands on the floor out to the side, about hip-width (est.) from the bench, toes forward, knee softly bent.
Back position. Hips and shoulders level, back roughly parallel to the floor in the bench version (a gentle slope is fine), spine long from tailbone to head, ribs down.
Neck. Gaze at the floor a hand-width ahead of the bench; the back of the neck is long, not looking up.
Grip. Hold the dumbbell with a firm overhand or neutral grip (palm facing the bench). The arm hangs straight down from the shoulder, dumbbell below the shoulder, not out in front.
Shoulder blade. Slide the working shoulder blade gently down and back before the first pull ("back pocket" cue), so the shoulder is not shrugged toward the ear.
Choose the weight. The lightest weight that lets you do 10 clean, slow reps with 3-4 left in the tank (section 7).

Camera. Phone in landscape at about hip-to-waist height (80-100 cm, est.), 2-2.5 m away. A side view shows the back line and elbow path; a front-three-quarter view shows trunk twist. Full body in frame.
Warm up 3-5 minutes (est.): march on the spot, arm circles, a few cat-cow movements (Yoga & Stretch 10), 6-8 bodyweight hinges, and one set of 6 reps with a very light weight or an empty hand.

steps.title: Get on the bench
steps.action: Place the left hand and left knee on the bench, the right foot on the floor, the back flat.
steps.feel: A stable three-point base; weight spread evenly.
steps.visualCheck: Side: back roughly level, head in line with the spine. Front: shoulders and hips level, not tilted.

steps.title: Pick the dumbbell up safely
steps.action: Before you get on the bench, stand with the dumbbell beside the bench, bend the knees and hips to pick it up with a flat back, then hold it as you set your hand and knee. Or have it on the floor and reach down with the working hand once you are in position.
steps.feel: Legs doing the lift, not the back.
steps.visualCheck: Side: back flat; no hunched pickup.

steps.title: Hang the arm and set the shoulder
steps.action: Let the arm hang straight down, shoulder blade slid gently down and back, ribs down, tummy lightly tight.
steps.feel: A long, firm torso; a mild stretch along the side of the back.
steps.visualCheck: Side: dumbbell directly under the shoulder. Front: shoulders level, no hunch, shoulder not shrugged.

steps.title: Pull the elbow toward the hip
steps.action: Lead with the elbow, not the hand: draw the elbow up and back toward the hip, keeping it fairly close to the body (sources prefer "toward the hip"; some say "back and up").
steps.feel: The mid-back and the wide back muscle shortening; the biceps helping but not leading.
steps.breathing: Breathe out as you pull (ACE gives exhale on the pull, snippet).
steps.visualCheck: Side: the elbow travels up and back in a smooth arc to just above the back line; the dumbbell ends near the lower ribs or hip. Front-three-quarter: shoulders and hips stay square to the floor.

steps.title: Keep the torso still
steps.action: Do not twist or lift the chest on the working side; keep both shoulders and both hips level with the floor.
steps.feel: The trunk muscles working to stay still, like a table top.
steps.breathing: Keep breathing; do not hold the breath.
steps.visualCheck: Front-three-quarter: the line between the shoulders stays level and stays parallel to the line between the hips; the back stays flat in the side view.

steps.title: Pause and squeeze
steps.action: At the top, the elbow is near the hip and slightly above the back line; stop for a beat and squeeze the shoulder blade gently toward the spine; do not shrug.
steps.feel: A gentle squeeze between the shoulder blade and the spine, shoulder away from the ear.
steps.visualCheck: Side: elbow bent roughly 90 degrees or less (est.), upper arm roughly in line with the back; no neck craning. Front: shoulder low.

steps.title: Lower under control
steps.action: Straighten the arm slowly back to hanging, letting the shoulder blade glide forward slightly at the bottom; do not drop.
steps.feel: A controlled stretch along the side of the back.
steps.visualCheck: Side: dumbbell travels in the same path back down; arm nearly straight at the bottom; the back stays flat. Front: shoulders level.

steps.title: Repeat for all reps, then change sides
steps.action: Do all the reps with one arm, set the dumbbell down gently, swap hand and knee, and do the same for the other arm. Start with the weaker arm and match its reps on the other side (a coaching tip, snippet).
steps.visualCheck: Both arms follow the same path and range.

steps.title: Set the dumbbell down safely
steps.action: After the last rep, lower the dumbbell to the floor on the towel or mat with a 2-3 s count, then step off the bench; do not drop it.
steps.feel: Controlled arm and legs, no back rounding.
steps.visualCheck: Side: back flat while lowering; the only sound is a soft touch.

commonMistakes.title: Twisting the torso to lift the weight
commonMistakes.text: Twisting the torso to lift the weight. Why: shifts work from the back to the trunk and shoulder (Livestrong, Fitness and Power, ACE, snippets); sources call it among the most common errors. Fix: lighter weight, hips and shoulders pointing at the floor, film from the front; slow the pull.

commonMistakes.title: Rounding or over-arching the back
commonMistakes.text: Rounding or over-arching the back. Why: puts pressure on the spine; sources call back arching the most common row error (snippets). Fix: lighter weight, a higher support surface, tummy lightly tight, eyes on the floor.

commonMistakes.title: Shrugging the shoulder toward the ear
commonMistakes.text: Shrugging the shoulder toward the ear. Why: the upper trapezius and neck take over (snippets). Fix: slide the shoulder blade down and back first; lead with the elbow, not the hand.

commonMistakes.title: Jerking or heaving the weight (momentum)
commonMistakes.text: Jerking or heaving the weight (momentum). Why: lets the swing do the work and invites back strain (NFPT, snippet). Fix: 2 s pull, 1 s pause, 3 s lower; reduce the weight.

commonMistakes.title: Weight too heavy, causing compensation
commonMistakes.text: Weight too heavy, causing compensation. Why: forces twisting, rounding and a short range (snippet). Fix: choose the weight by 3-4 reps in reserve (section 7).

commonMistakes.title: Pulling the hand to the chest instead of the elbow toward the hip
commonMistakes.text: Pulling the hand to the chest instead of the elbow toward the hip. Why: it turns the movement into an arm curl and a shoulder shrug. Fix: think "elbow to hip pocket"; dumbbell ends near the lower ribs.

commonMistakes.title: Not lowering fully (half reps)
commonMistakes.text: Not lowering fully (half reps). Why: short range cuts the stretch and the work; the arm should hang nearly straight at the bottom. Fix: let the arm straighten at the bottom with the shoulder blade moving slightly forward.

commonMistakes.title: Locking the supporting elbow or leaning heavily on the support
commonMistakes.text: Locking the supporting elbow or leaning heavily on the support. Why: the shoulder gets stuck and the torso twists. Fix: soft support elbow; on the thigh version, light touch.

commonMistakes.title: Dropping the dumbbell at the end or letting it hit the floor
commonMistakes.text: Dropping the dumbbell at the end or letting it hit the floor. Why: noise for neighbours below and risk to feet. Fix: lower it with a 2-3 s count onto a mat or towel; keep feet clear.

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath. Why: raises blood pressure and brings dizziness (breathing study PubMed 7741618, carried from earlier items). Fix: breathe out on the pull, in on the lowering.

safetyNotes: Lower back problems: the supported version with a high support surface takes load off the back; one source suggests more supported variations and lighter loads for anyone with a history of low back pain (snippet); stop if pain increases or spreads down a leg. Clinical guidance specific to the weighted one-arm row: Not found.

Shoulder problems: rowing can aggravate the shoulder if it does not track cleanly; sources suggest a lighter dumbbell, a shorter range, or a band row, and to pause until a clinician clears you if pain flares (snippets); stop with pinching or sharp pain. Clinical guidance: Not found.
Neck pain: a shrug or craning neck during the row can irritate the neck; lower the weight and cue the shoulder down (snippet).
Knee problems: the bench version loads one knee; use a cushion, or use the staggered-stance or chair version. RDL-style knee guidance: Not found.

High blood pressure and heart disease: breathe out on the pull; do not hold the breath; light weight and moderate effort; get medical clearance first if you have heart disease or uncontrolled blood pressure.

Osteoporosis: loaded strength work is generally recommended; avoid loaded spinal rounding and twisting; with severe osteoporosis or a prior vertebral fracture, ask a clinician first (reviews, snippets).

Pregnancy and postpartum: resistance training is commonly recommended for uncomplicated pregnancies (snippet); the standing or hand-supported version avoids lying flat; ACOG's own wording was not reached, so ask your obstetrician, midwife or women's health physiotherapist; stop with dizziness, pelvic heaviness, leaking or pain.

Mumbai flat: put the bench or chair on a non-slip mat or against a wall; set the dumbbell down gently on a mat or towel; do not drop it on a tile floor; no glass bottles; use a towel row only on a solid door and handle, never a hollow or loose one; avoid the balcony slab.
